models.architecture_or_algorithm: Variational autoencoder (VAE) for generation, combined with regression models (GB, RF, LGBM, XGB) for MIC prediction
models.candidate_reason: Provides both generative and predictive components for AMP activity; regression models trained on public data and experimentally validated

models.architecture_or_algorithm: Pre-trained language model embeddings + convolutional neural network (CNN)
models.input_features: Contextualized embeddings of amino acid sequences from pre-trained language models
models.candidate_reason: Novel input representation using pre-trained language models; code and data publicly available; outperforms previous state-of-the-art

models.architecture_or_algorithm: Support vector machine (SVM) with LZ-complexity pairwise kernel, integrated with sequence alignment
models.input_features: LZ-complexity pairwise similarity measure from amino acid sequences
models.candidate_reason: Method for AMP prediction with reported sensitivity; could be included in benchmarks if implementation becomes available

models.architecture_or_algorithm: PyAMPA contains 5 modules: AMPScreen (sliding window propensity scoring), AMPValidate (RF classifier with 2-mer vectors), AMPSolve (RF for hemolysis/toxicity; RF regression for 11 strains; multivariate regression for half-life), AMPMutate (systematic point mutation scan), AMPOptimize (genetic algorithm multi-objective optimization of antimicrobial activity, half-life, hemolysis)
models.input_features: Amino acid sequences, 2-mer features, proportion of nonpolar residues, presence of Trp/Tyr, isoelectric point, etc.
models.dataset_source_or_link: AMPlify dataset, Liu et al. CPP database, AMPDeep hemolytic database, ToxinPred toxicity database, GRAMPA dataset (https://github.com/zswitten/Antimicrobial-Peptides)
models.candidate_reason: Comprehensive AMP discovery platform with screening, validation, property prediction, and optimization; uses random forest and genetic algorithms; experimentally validated on 10 novel peptides

datasets.dataset_source: Liu et al. cell-penetrating peptide database
datasets.evidence: For cell-penetrating peptides (CPPs), the Liu et al. database was used, containing 924 sequences, of which 462 positive and 462 negative CPPs.
To predict hemolytic peptides, we used the AMPDeep database of 7,180 peptides, of which 3,007 hemolytic and 4,173 non-hemolytic.
For toxicity prediction, we used the ToxinPred database, with 3,613 peptides, of which 1,156 toxic and 2,457 non-toxic.

important_evidence: PepVAE code not publicly available, only 'available upon request', but dataset and MIC prediction models are described.
LMPred provides full code and data, outperforms previous state-of-the-art.
SVM-LZ paper lacks code; full-text cache mismatch needs verification.
PyAMPA is a comprehensive platform with code, multiple modules, and experimental validation of 10 novel peptides.
uncertainties: The full-text cache for PMID 25802839 (doi:10.1093/nar/gkn823) appears to correspond to a different article about APD2 database, not the SVM-LZ prediction method. Need to verify the actual paper content.
PepVAE model weights are not publicly available; only 'available upon request'. Is it still a candidate for benchmark if code cannot be obtained?
The LMPred paper's full-text excerpt contained unrelated RNA secondary structure content; verify that the actual paper matches the abstract.
